ud6.10:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then at that time venerable Ānanda
ud6.10:1.3: went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side.
ud6.10:1.4: While sat on one side venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
ud6.10:2.1: “For as long as the Realised Ones, reverend Sir, do not arise in the world, the Worthy Ones, the Perfect Sambuddhas, for that long the wanderers from other sects are venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud6.10:2.2: But when the Realised Ones, reverend Sir, do arise in the world, the Worthy Ones, the Perfect Sambuddhas, then the wanderers from other sects are not venerated, not respected, not revered, not honoured, not esteemed, and are not in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud6.10:2.3: Now, reverend Sir, the Fortunate One is venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick, and (so is) the Community of monks.”
ud6.10:3.1: “Just so, Ānanda, for as long as the Realised Ones, Ānanda, do not arise in the world, the Worthy Ones, the Perfect Sambuddhas, for that long the wanderers from other sects are venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud6.10:3.2: But when the Realised Ones, Ānanda, do arise in the world, the Worthy Ones, the Perfect Sambuddhas, then the wanderers from other sects are not venerated, not respected, not revered, not honoured, not esteemed, and are not in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick.
ud6.10:3.3: Now the Realised One is venerated, respected, revered, honoured, esteemed, and in receipt of robes, almsfood, dwellings, and medicinal requisites to help when sick, and (so is) the Community of monks.”
ud6.10:4.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud6.10:5.2: for as long as the light-maker (the sun) does not rise,
ud6.10:5.3: But when the brilliant one (the sun) has risen,
ud6.10:5.4: The (glow worm’s) light is destroyed, and does not shine forth.
ud6.10:6.1: In the same way the reasoners shine forth
ud6.10:6.2: for as long as the Perfect Sambuddhas do not arise in the world.
ud6.10:6.3: The reasoners are not purified, nor are their disciples,
ud6.10:6.4: of wrong view, they are not released from suffering.”
